claims.claim: P4: x-polarized (Standard Model) and p-polarized (χ) matter both couple universally to H, and gauge forces do not cross polarizations. Taken strictly since v2.1: no kinetic mixing beyond what gravity induces, ε ≲ 10⁻¹³, and zero if hidden charge conjugation is exact.

claims.claim: Under strict P4, a conjugate monopole carries no charge under our photon and has no gauge coupling to our matter. Gravity is the only coupling guaranteed: on the vacuum slice H = diag(g, g⁻¹), and χ propagates on g.

claims.claim: The 't Hooft–Polyakov monopole: SU(2) → U(1) by an adjoint scalar gives π₂(S²) = ℤ monopoles of charge 4π/g_d and mass M = 4πf v/g_d, with f between 1 (BPS) and about 1.79. The value 1.79 is not in #14's cited [16], but the referee confirmed it numerically.

claims.claim: #14 §2: an exact mirror copy of the Standard Model has no stable monopoles, because the electroweak vacuum manifold is S³ and π₂ = 0, so a hidden sector with monopoles must differ from ours. The topology is not what failed.

claims.claim: Witten effect, ruling 9 ('Accepted, not re-checked'): with kinetic mixing and a physical hidden θ, the candidate's monopoles carry a visible electric charge of about εθ/2π · e. That contradicts #14 v3's statement that the constraints act on ψ, not the dark matter, which is now dead. Decision 1 (strict sector separation) closed this channel together with ψ's millicharge and re-thermalization.
claims.quote: With mixing and a physical hidden θ, the monopoles carry visible electric charge ~ εθ/2π · e (Witten effect) | Accepted, not re-checked

claims.claim: The monopole problem (Preskill): superheavy monopoles are unacceptably abundant, annihilation cannot lower n/T³ below about 10⁻¹⁰ at 10¹⁶ GeV, and inflation is the remedy. Ruling 10 holds that annihilation at α_m ≈ 34 is Preskill's Dirac case, already worked out for hidden sectors.
claims.tag: [T]; ruling 10, upheld at the level of the abstracts
claims.quote: Annihilation at α_m ≈ 34 is Preskill's Dirac case, already done for hidden sectors

claims.claim: Hidden-sector monopoles avoid overclosure only for breaking scales ≲ 100 PeV or with early matter domination. Below that scale, annihilation in the hidden plasma sets the abundance: the established topological-dark-matter scenario, which does not depend on Born reciprocity.
claims.quote: Below that scale, annihilation in the hidden plasma sets the abundance. That is the established topological-dark-matter scenario [28S, 29S], and nothing in it depends on Born reciprocity.

claims.claim: #14 used the Parker, extended Parker and MACRO bounds only counterfactually: had its monopoles carried our magnetic charge, the dark-matter flux would exceed the bounds by 7.5 to 12 orders, so sector separation was mandatory.

Section 11 (charge lattice) is added. The monopole audit splits supposition 5, row 8's observable becomes 'Magnetic monopoles (ours)', and conjugate solitons of a p-local gauge sector are proposed as a third dark-matter candidate.
The α_d-from-our-DSZ contradiction is a valid kill. The 'knots' are renamed π₂ monopole-class, the Preskill citation is fixed, and the toy-Lagrangian demand becomes acceptance criterion #1.

Verdict B near B/C. The weakest link is the α_d derivation ('matrix coincidence ≠ physical identity', 'numerology'); the referee also poses the SUSY-exactness burden and requests the extended Parker bound.

The HANDOFF lists the charge-lattice identification and the π₂ soliton candidate as alive and the explanation of non-detection as dead. It lists #12, which contains the magnetic identification, as the 'final (destination article)'.

Paul decides that S-duality no longer fixes α_d (worklog F2). #14 v3 is drafted with Dirac quantization applied only to the hidden sector's own charges and the charge-lattice identification used 'only as motivation'.
Worklog O3: Paul raises the two dual cones of #13; the dark sector is kept in ordinary kinematics.

Round 3, verdict C. Rulings 1 and 3 (Kibble), 9 (Witten-effect charge, accepted without re-checking), 10 (Preskill's Dirac case) and 12 (normalization, minor). Decision 1 adopts strict sector separation, Decision 2 retires the soliton candidate, Decision 3 drops the √N floor.

tensions.description: Inside #11: §11.1 says 'true but irrelevant' is 'the empty set', while App. A item 5 records P.R.'s phrase as 'measure zero'. The checkpoint does not reconcile them; the verdict is the same under either.

Inside #11: §14 item 8 says the soliton-spectrum and p-localization items are 'closed by the §12 obituary', but §12 says the topological clumping loophole 'remains untested, but has no candidate' and App. A item 3 calls it untested.

Flag 28: #11 §11.2 writes '4π/e² ≈ 34' beside e·g ~ 2π. With α = e²/4π that expression is 1/α ≈ 137; the 34 is π/e² = 1/(4α). The flag is confirmed and awaits Paul's ruling; the wiki quotes #11 unchanged.

The HANDOFF ties the alive ontology to the soliton candidate ('As ontology they're alive (the soliton candidate)'), while #11 keeps the ontology alive and retires the candidacy. The wiki resolves this by precedence in #11's favour.

The electric-sublattice clause appears in the HANDOFF's open item 1 and in #14's criterion (1), but #11 §14 item 11, the worklog's S0–S5 criteria and the root CLAUDE.md ('done to the referees' wording') omit it and declare the criterion met. Within the wiki, the OP8 page folds the clause as an 'Open:' section (and the section hub lists it as open), while the acceptance-criterion page heads it without 'Open:', says no current document lists it as open, and the toy-models hub strip does not list it.
README.md still describes the program as explaining 'missing magnetic monopoles', against HANDOFF §2 and #11 §11.1, which list that explanation as dead (flag 37, confirmed, no ruling).

#12 says the momentum-polarized sector is the magnetic side of electromagnetism. That conflicts with strict P4, with the HANDOFF ('dark by sector separation', not magnetically charged under our photon), with #14 v3 ('These objects carry no charge under our photon'), with row 7 and with the dead α_d ≈ 34. The wiki records #12's claim as dead by its own reading; no program document or review rules on it, although the wiki's rules say status comes from #11.

#14 v2 identified the momentum-polarized matter sector as the S-dual image of the electric sector, with reciprocity acting as modular S. #14 v3 kept the shared matrix 'only as motivation', and #11 §11.3 keeps a structural observation plus an [O] conjecture with no claim about couplings or hidden sectors. The stronger form was superseded by Paul's decision of 2026-10-19.

#11's plain-language and assessment wording ('Two intuitions, one operation'; 'polarization of phase space and of charge space as one move') can be read as the content of the [O] conjecture. §11.3 tags only the same-operation identity [D — structural] and leaves 'one structure' as [O]. #12 takes the stronger reading without the [O].

The weak-to-strong result (a weakly coupled hidden sector has strongly coupled monopoles) is listed among the survivors in #11 §12 but not in the round-3 adjudication's own 'What survives v3' list. The wiki follows the checkpoint by precedence.

Normalization: Zwanziger's abstract states the pairing in 4πℤ, while #14 and #11 write 2πℤ, and Schwinger was uncited in #14. Ruling 12 accepted both as minor citation issues; #11's [17]† lists Schwinger.

Is the monopole sector conjugate matter at all? v2.0 called it a 'p-local gauge sector', and the wiki glosses conjugate-sector solitons as made of the p-polarized fields χ. But #14 described its hidden sector with ordinary relativistic quantum field theory, and worklog O3 records that #14's dark sector was never reconciled with #13's dual kinematics.

Flag 21: ruling 3 attributes '1e9–1e12 overproduction' to the referee's Kibble–Zurek integration, which printed 1.1e12–2.2e12; the 1e9 lower end is the LMW analytic estimate. Confirmed, unruled; the verdict is unaffected.

Two overproduction ranges for the old benchmark appear in the record. The monopole-problem page quotes the referee's 4.9e3–9.8e4, which depends on the hidden-sector temperature ratio (ξ = 0.76..0.5). #11 §12, ruling 2 and verify/soliton_obituary.py give the gated 2.1×10³–1.2×10⁴ [V]. The inputs differ, and the monopole-problem page does not set the two side by side; partition F1's overproduction page covers both.

The wiki tags as [D] the statement that under strict P4 conjugate monopoles carry no charge under our photon. #11 §11.1's [D] covers only that they gravitate. The no-charge clause follows from P4, which is [P], and the record states it explicitly only for #14's hidden sector (HANDOFF §2, #14 v3 §2).
Citation gaps in §11: the label '17†-adjacent' is unexplained (reference [17] is the DSZ trio, not Montonen–Olive), and the phrase 'in the literature's own words' carries no citation.

Terminology: the HANDOFF §6 and #14 v2 rename the objects 'π₂ monopole-class', distinct from π₃ Hopfion knots, while #11's plain-language passages (§9, §12) and #12 still say 'knots' for the π₂ monopoles.

readers.summary:
Partition E treats monopoles themselves as established physics [T]: Dirac quantization and the DSZ pairing, the 't Hooft–Polyakov monopole, the Witten effect, the Kibble mechanism, the monopole problem with inflation as its remedy, and the Parker and MACRO bounds. On top of that it holds four program claims.

1. Founding supposition 5, "Monopoles live in conjugate space, explaining non-detection", is split by #11 §11.1 [D]. As an explanation it is dead: "the relevant duality is electric–magnetic ..., not x↔p, and inflationary dilution already accounts for absence [T]". As ontology it is alive: "by P4, conjugate-sector solitons gravitate".
2. Row 8 keeps an untagged permanent null for "Magnetic monopoles (ours)", with Weyl-semimetal Berry-curvature monopoles [16†] as "the only shadow". Its account of the absence is dilution [T], not the program's own physics.
3. The magnetic mirror-family is absorbed as established physics. Non-observation is "structural" (Dirac's strong coupling ≈ 34; the formula beside it is under flag 28), and #11 parallels the hidden magnetic half with the hidden second metric X of §7.
4. §11.3 [D — structural; math T]: the charge lattice is symplectic, a duality frame is a Lagrangian polarization, and one matrix generates ρ, Z → −Z⁻¹ and S.

On monopoles and comatter, the live record keeps the two separate. Strict P4 ("gauge forces do not cross polarizations", ε ≲ 10⁻¹³) leaves conjugate monopoles, if they exist, coupled to us by gravity only, and #11 does not specify the p-sector's gauge structure. The only bridge is the structural identification plus OP8, the unqueued [O] conjecture of one enlarged modular structure. No Lagrangian relates the two choices, no script checks the charge side, and the electric-sublattice clause of acceptance criterion 1 is unaddressed.

The stronger identifications are superseded or dead: #14 v2's "momentum-polarized matter sector is the S-dual image of the electric sector" (superseded by Paul's decision of 2026-10-19; #14 withdrawn), and #12's "magnetic side of electromagnetism" (popsci-only, recorded dead by the wiki's own reading).

readers.summary:
Partition D adds no new monopole physics. It is the error-and-ruling record on the documents' monopole passages, and every relevant flag is audited and unruled. All 44 worksheet entries carry unticked ruling boxes, and 'Nothing in the sources changes until Paul rules.'

Flag 28: #11 §11.2's 'Dirac's condition e·g ~ 2π pins the magnetic coupling near 4π/e² ≈ 34' has the right number and the wrong formula. The 34 is g²/4π = π/e² = 1/(4α) ≈ 34.26. 4π/e² = 1/α ≈ 137 is the e·g = 4π value (Schwinger/'t Hooft–Polyakov, S-dual). 'This 34 is our own magnetic coupling, distinct from the dead α_d ≈ 34 of the soliton episode.' Its audit scripts are not gated.

Flag 37: the README still says the program explains 'missing magnetic monopoles'. HANDOFF §2 and #11 §11.1 list conjugate monopoles as that explanation as dead ('wrong duality; inflation suffices').

Flags 33–34: verify/soliton_obituary.py is the only gated monopole-related script (Kibble p = 104, M* = 2.9–4.4×10¹² GeV, overproduction 2.1×10³–1.2×10⁴, W'± overclosure 10¹⁶–10¹⁷, the ψ window), and it claims more coverage than it has. claims.claim: v2.0 of #11 listed 'topological solitons of a p-local gauge sector (§11)' as a third dark-matter candidate, stable by topological charge, alongside χ particles and the X-condensate. #14 developed it into superheavy 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles of a hidden SU(2) → U(1) sector (#11 §12).
claims.quote: superheavy 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles of a hidden SU(2) → U(1) sector

claims.claim: Naming history. v1 called the objects 'knots', and round 1 renamed them 'π₂ monopole-class'. v2 required only an unnamed G broken to H with π₂(G/H) nonzero. Round 2 asked for an explicit group ('dual SU(2)→U(1) suffices'), and v3 supplied one.
claims.quote: supporting "monopole-class defects classified by pi_2, not knot solitons in the pi_3/Hopfion sense"

claims.claim: The candidate's monopoles were magnetically charged under the hidden U(1)_d only, never under our electromagnetism. #14 v3 §2 'What is not asserted' states the opposite of v1's approach: 'nothing is quantized against our gauge field' (alpha-d-coupling.md:56).
claims.quote: The candidate's monopoles carry magnetic charge under the hidden U(1)_d only.

claims.claim: #14 v3 §2 sets the magnetic charge inside the hidden sector: g_m = 4π/g_d, the Dirac minimum relative to ψ's charge g_d/2, the smallest hidden charge. So α_m = 1/α_W′ for any g_d, 'the strong magnetic coupling is generic, not a hypothesis'. The referee's script prints α_m·α_W′ = 1.000000.
claims.quote: Its monopoles carry magnetic charge g_m = 4 pi/g_d, the Dirac minimum relative to psi's charge g_d/2, so their mutual coupling is alpha_m = g_m^2/4pi = 1/alpha_W' [7].

claims.claim: v3's abstract identified the hidden SU(2) sector with the momentum-polarized half of broken Born reciprocity, and summarized the candidate as 'stable by topology, dark by sector separation, effectively collisionless, and inaccessible to direct detection'. #14 §2's sector definition opens 'The momentum-polarized matter sector contains a gauge group SU(2)_d'.
claims.quote: The hidden sector is identified with the momentum-polarized half of a spontaneously broken Born reciprocity.

claims.claim: #14 §6 lists 'the identification of the SU(2)_d sector as the momentum-polarized matter sector' among its Conjectural claims, together with hypothesis H and the colder reheating (obituary.md:175). #14 §2 marks the sector itself '(postulated)'.
claims.quote: #14 §6 listed that identification as "Conjectural".

claims.claim: #14 used the charge-lattice correspondence (DSZ pairing symplectic, duality frame = Lagrangian polarization, same matrix as the Born rotation) only as motivation for the sector, and no number depended on it. #14 §2, resolved: it 'suggests that the vacuum event that polarizes phase space also fixes which description of a gauge sector is the electric one'. The wiki says the model was not refuted; what died is the claim that the program had selected it. It calls this the soliton episode's instance of the 'framework does no work' critique.
claims.quote: its charge-lattice motivation for the sector was used "only as motivation", and "No numerical result below depends on it" (#14 §2).

claims.claim: Wiki gloss: a 'p-local gauge sector' is a gauge force of the momentum-polarized matter, the mirror half of the program's matter under P4. #11 uses the phrase only at §12 (line 139, '(§11)'), and §11 never uses it. The gloss matches #14's sector definition, so it goes beyond #11's text without contradicting it.
claims.quote: A p-local gauge sector is a gauge force of the momentum-polarized matter, the mirror half of the program's matter content under postulate P4 [link markup removed]

claims.claim: Cross-reference resolved from obituary.md:153. #11 v2.1's technical abstract says the electric–magnetic charge lattice with its DSZ pairing [17†] is a second arena where the same polarization choice recurs, and that the retired soliton candidate was 'motivated' by it. The wiki quotes only the retirement clause.
claims.quote: furnishes a second arena in which the same polarization choice recurs. A third dark-sector candidate it motivated — superheavy topological solitons of a hidden gauge sector — was retired

claims.claim: #14's acceptance criterion 1 asked for an action in which ρ is a genuine Noether symmetry, spontaneously broken, with η selecting both the position polarization and the hidden sector's electric description. The toy models met the first half 'in the referees' wording' (#11 §14 item 11) but do not address the second. HANDOFF §2 open item 1 (HANDOFF.md:35) phrased the second half as η 'also selecting the electric sublattice'.
claims.quote: which do not address its second half, η selecting "the hidden sector's electric description"

claims.claim: #14's second tie to the program was sector separation, postulated: no field carries charge under both U(1)_d and our hypercharge. Since v2.1 the program carries it as P4 taken strictly (Decision 1).
claims.quote: The second is sector separation, also marked "(postulated)": "No field carries charge under both U(1)_d and our hypercharge" (#14 §2).

claims.claim: HANDOFF §2, written before round 3, listed the soliton candidate among live results: dark by sector separation and not magnetically charged under our photon. It sat in the same bullet as the charge-lattice identification (HANDOFF.md:26). Superseded by #11 §12, the adjudication and the root CLAUDE.md.
claims.quote: Current best DM candidate: superheavy (~10¹³–10¹⁷ GeV) topological solitons (π₂ monopole-class) of a separate, strongly coupled dual gauge sector

claims.claim: #14 §4 'Not monopoles of our U(1)': monopoles magnetic under our electromagnetism would exceed the Parker bound by 7.5 orders, MACRO by 8 and the extended Parker bound by 12, so 'Sector separation is therefore mandatory'. The referee confirmed 7.50, 8.06 and 12.03. Worklog L1 keeps Parker and MACRO only as the reason separation is needed. #14 exclusion condition 2 was a confirmed monopole flux of our U(1) at dark-matter abundance. The arithmetic survives v3 but is not in the current gate.
claims.quote: If these objects carried magnetic charge under our electromagnetism, they would be classic monopoles and excluded. The flux at dark-matter density would be F = n v/4 pi ~ 3e-8 /cm^2/s/sr.

claims.claim: Three flux limits frame the counterfactual. The Parker bound requires monopoles not to drain the Galactic field. The extended Parker bound applies the same argument to the young Galaxy's seed field and scales with mass. MACRO searched directly. The referee found each figure supported by its source: PDG 2024 eq. 95.9, MACRO Table 2 and Adams et al. 1993. Worklog R3 adds charge scaling (g/g_D)⁻² at high mass and (g/g_D)⁻¹ at low mass (Kobayashi–Perri 2023).
claims.quote: the Parker bound requires that monopoles accelerated by the Galaxy's magnetic field not drain the field faster than it regenerates

claims.claim: Point (c): while U(1)_d is unbroken (massless hidden photon), kinetic mixing gives hidden monopoles no visible magnetic flux (Hiramatsu–Ibe–Suzuki–Yamaguchi). Brümmer–Jaeckel: 'hidden monopoles are invisible to ordinary electrically charged matter'. Minicharged, flux-tube-confined monopoles need a massive dark photon (Terning–Verhaaren), which #14 excludes. The referee marked it SUPPORTED, and the adjudication lists it among what survives v3.
claims.quote: With U(1)_d unbroken, kinetic mixing does not give the monopoles magnetic charge under our photon: the hidden monopole induces no visible magnetic flux even with epsilon nonzero [12, 10]. Minicharged monopoles would require a massive hidden photon [13]

claims.claim: v2 assumed that mixing ε gives the solitons magnetic charge εg under our photon. Worklog L1 found this wrong for v2's own massless-dark-photon setup and counted four places in v2 resting on it, which v3 rewrote.
claims.quote: So v2's premise, "mixing ε gives the solitons magnetic charge εg under our photon", "is wrong for its own setup."

claims.claim: Witten effect: a physical hidden angle θ_d makes the monopoles hidden dyons, and with ε ≠ 0 they carry a small visible electric charge (Brümmer–Jaeckel–Khoze eq. 3.19, per the referee). The referee called it 'Phenomenologically tiny at M=3e13 GeV', but it makes exclusion condition 1 self-triggering. It contradicts v3's 'constraints act on ψ, not the dark matter' whenever ε ≠ 0. Decision 1 closed the channel.
claims.quote: Ruling 9, "Accepted, not re-checked": "With mixing and a physical hidden θ, the monopoles carry visible electric charge ~ εθ/2π · e (Witten effect)"

claims.claim: #11 §4: P4, 'gauge forces do not cross polarizations', is taken strictly since v2.1. No kinetic mixing beyond what gravity induces: none if hidden C is exact, otherwise from six loops, ε ≲ 10⁻¹³.
claims.quote: [P; taken strictly since v2.1: no kinetic mixing between the sectors beyond what gravity induces, which vanishes if hidden charge conjugation is exact and otherwise first appears at six loops, ε ≲ 10⁻¹³ [27S].]

claims.claim: Round-3 Decision 1 (2026-10-19) chose strict sector separation: ε ≲ 10⁻¹³ from gravity alone, and zero if hidden C is gauged. It takes P4 at face value. The dimension-5 alternative's 'O(1) at the Planck scale' coefficient has no source. The root CLAUDE.md records 'Strict sector separation (P4 at face value) is in force.'
claims.quote: It costs nothing and closes three failure channels at once: ψ millicharge, the monopoles' Witten-effect charge (ruling 9), and re-thermalization of the hidden sector.

claims.claim: The wiki's reading: Decision 1 is a decision about the postulate, not a derivation. The UV stability of sector separation was never computed, and HANDOFF §2 open item 3 ('UV stability of sector separation / kinetic mixing') was settled by taking P4 strictly.
claims.quote: It is a decision about the postulate, not a derivation: whether sector separation is stable against quantum corrections was never computed

claims.claim: Point (a): gravity alone induces no mixing if hidden C is exact, and otherwise only at six loops or more, ε ≲ 10⁻¹³ (Gherghetta–Kersten–Olive–Pospelov). Point (b): a discrete symmetry acting as hidden C forbids the dimension-5 operator only if gauged, since quantum gravity is believed to admit no exact global symmetries (Banks–Seiberg; Harlow–Ooguri). The referee: 'SUPPORTS both parts'. Point (a) survives v3.
claims.quote: Kinetic mixing vanishes to all perturbative orders if hidden charge conjugation is an exact symmetry. If it is broken, gravity can induce mixing, but only at six loops or more, giving epsilon <~ 1e-13 [9].

claims.claim: The referee notes that Gherghetta et al. present 10⁻¹³ as a floor, 'minimum kinetic mixing in any theory with hidden gauge interactions and charge symmetry breaking'. That fits P4's '≲' only in the sense 'up to'. The reading is unresolved.
claims.quote: #11's "ε ≲ 10⁻¹³" stands as written; the reading is flagged and not resolved

claims.claim: The kinetic-mixing page's used-by entry for 'Conjugate monopoles as ontology' says that under strict P4 a conjugate monopole carries no charge under our photon.
claims.quote: under strict P4 a conjugate monopole carries no charge under our photon

claims.claim: #11 §11.1 [D]: conjugate monopoles as ontology are alive, since by P4 conjugate-sector solitons gravitate, while their candidacy as the dark matter is retired in v2.1. The soliton index calls this 'the surviving claim that conjugate-sector monopoles, if they exist, gravitate' (_index.md:39). The Bullet Cluster page: 'whatever the conjugate sector contains gravitates' (bullet-cluster.md:121).
claims.quote: The ontology of conjugate monopoles is alive: "by P4, conjugate-sector solitons gravitate", while "Their candidacy as the dark matter itself is retired in v2.1 (§12)"

claims.claim: Cross-reference resolved from obituary.md:165's citation of #11 §11.1. As an explanation of our monopole null result, conjugate monopoles are dead: the relevant duality is electric–magnetic, not x↔p, and inflation accounts for absence. The partition's pages quote only the ontology half of §11.1.
claims.quote: As an explanation of the null result: dead — the relevant duality is electric–magnetic (E↔B, g → 1/g), not x↔p, and inflationary dilution already accounts for absence [T].

claims.claim: Topological dark matter, standard physics: SU(2) broken to U(1) by an adjoint scalar has an S² of vacua, which supports 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles. A monopole cannot decay; only monopole–antimonopole pairs annihilate. A hidden sector that does not couple to ours touches ordinary matter only through gravity.
claims.quote: If the hidden sector does not couple to ours, its monopoles interact with ordinary matter only through gravity, which is what dark matter requires.

claims.claim: Popular article #12 uses 'about 34, against our 1/137' for the claim that the momentum-polarized sector is 'the magnetic side of electromagnetism'. The wiki records the claim as popsci-only and dead (Obituary: the magnetic identification), and as contradicting strict sector separation (kinetic-mixing.md:173).
claims.quote: for the claim that the momentum-polarized sector is "the magnetic side of electromagnetism". That claim appears only in the popular article and is dead

claims.claim: The popular articles still present the candidate as live. #10 has a three-way question. #12 says three requirements (thirteen-billion-year stability, the strong coupling Dirac's condition demands, transparency to light) 'select the same corner', quoting v2-benchmark figures. Popular articles are never a source for a claim's status.
claims.quote: topological knots — the conjugate sector's monopoles, unable to untie, which would explain dark matter's thirteen-billion-year stability for free

claims.claim: #11 §12, 'What survives': a weakly coupled hidden sector always has strongly coupled monopoles, by Dirac quantization. What died is every attempt to pick the particular value 34 for a hidden sector (alpha-d-coupling.md:127).
claims.quote: "A weakly coupled hidden sector always has strongly coupled monopoles, by Dirac quantization [T]."

claims.claim: Attempt 1 (#14 v1) fixed the coupling by Dirac quantization against our electron's charge. Round 1's valid kill: Dirac's argument applies only to charges coupled to the same gauge field, so the monopoles would be magnetic charges of our electromagnetism, which contradicts their darkness (the wiki's explanation, line 56).
claims.quote: α_d ≈ 34 via Dirac quantization against our photon (round-1 reviewer's valid kill: can't use our DSZ lattice and then deny coupling to our photon).

claims.claim: Attempt 2 (v2's load-bearing conjecture): the momentum-polarized sector is the S-dual image of the electric sector, its coupling fixed by 'the reciprocity map, acting as the modular S transformation' to α_d = 1/(4α) ~ 34. Round 2: 'matrix coincidence ≠ physical identity' / 'numerology'. R1: exact S-duality is tested only in N=4 SYM and finite N=2 theories, 'an expectation, not a no-go'. Paul set it aside on 2026-10-19. v3: 'Exact electric-magnetic duality is also not assumed'. No round-3 ruling addresses it, and #11 v2.2 does not mention it.
claims.quote: The two polarization choices are made by the same vacuum event, and the momentum-polarized matter sector is the S-dual image of the electric sector

claims.claim: Worklog F2: v2 used α_d = 34 both as the elementary coupling, which would make the solitons light, and as the monopole coupling. Resolution: the dual sector's elementary coupling is weak, the solitons heavy (M ≈ Λ_c/α_e,d), the monopoles strongly coupled. Then α_d ≈ 34 follows from 'a mirror-coupling equality' α_e,d ≈ α. Superseded because the hypothesis it led to died.
claims.quote: That factor is ~137 only if e_d²/4π ≈ 1/137. With e_d²/4π = α_d = 34 it is 0.029, so the solitons would not be heavy.

claims.claim: Attempt 3, hypothesis H (#14 v3 §2): (g_d/2)²/4π = α, so α_W′ = 4α ≈ 1/34 and α_m = 1/(4α) ≈ 34. #14 §6 lists it as Conjectural. Referee: 'motivated, not derived'; matching ψ to e/3 gives α_m = 308, and 'the framework gives no way to choose'. H died with v3 and is absent from both survivor lists.
claims.quote: The motivation is that reciprocity exchanges the two polarizations; if it acts on gauge couplings at all, the minimal action is to equate the elementary charges of the two sectors.

claims.claim: An exact mirror copy of the Standard Model has no stable monopoles because π₂(S³) = 0, so the hidden gauge structure must differ from ours. The worklog draws the consequence that 'H relates couplings only, not gauge groups' (hidden-sector.md:56).
claims.quote: An exact mirror copy of the Standard Model cannot serve: the electroweak vacuum manifold is S^3, whose pi_2 vanishes, so it has no stable monopoles.

claims.claim: The convention spread (worklog R2, 'adjudicated [V]'). One-loop running gives 29.0, 28.8 and 27.3 at 10¹¹, 3×10¹¹ and 10¹⁶ GeV; round 2's 'toward ~6–8' is not reproduced for α_em. The number is convention-dependent by a factor of 4. The referee also flagged Zwanziger's 4πZ against #14's 2πZ (ruling 12, accepted). 'With H dead, nothing in the program fixes α_d.'
claims.tag: [V] (worklog; predecessor script, not in current gate)
claims.quote: Convention: 1/(4α) = 34.26 (eg = 2πn) vs 1/α = 137.04 (eg = 4πn).

claims.claim: #11 §11.2 [T]: for our own electromagnetism, Dirac's condition puts the magnetic coupling near 34. This concerns our own magnetic charges, not a hidden sector. Flag 28: the number is right (1/(4α)), but the formula beside it, 4π/e², equals 1/α ≈ 137.
claims.quote: "Dirac's condition e·g ~ 2π pins the magnetic coupling near 4π/e² ≈ 34 — the magnetic world is our strong-coupling mirror, heavy and bound"

claims.claim: Kibble yield n/s = p (T_c/M_Pl)³: v2 used p = O(1), and v3 used p ≈ 0.023 while treating 'p = 1 as the upper end'. The worklog's F1 used 0.023.
claims.quote: The Kibble estimate n/s = p (T_c/M_Pl)³ had been normalized at p = 1 (#14 v2) and p ≈ 0.023 (#14 v3).

claims.claim: Ruling 3, upheld: the one-per-horizon count is a causal floor, supported by Murayama–Shu's abstract and LMW. The referee: p 'should be >= ~25-100, not <= 1'. v3's own §4 first-order transition implies bubble counting p ~ 10²–10⁸, 'flatly inconsistent' with 'p = 1 as the upper end'.
claims.quote: Ruling 3, upheld: "Kibble is a floor, not a ceiling; Kibble–Zurek or bubble counting add more".

claims.claim: v3's 'reduced-Planck factor of about 3' (3.350) came from swapping M_Pl while holding p fixed; consistently normalized, the two conventions agree, and the gate checks it. The referee: v3's reduced-Planck lower edge (2.74e12 GeV) was 'in fact the physically correct Kibble minimum (2.87e12)'.
claims.quote: Ruling 2: "The "reduced-Planck factor of 3" was not a convention spread: consistently normalized, the two conventions agree."

claims.claim: v3's script knot_numbers.py reproduced the wrong p and passed. Lesson 2 makes the replacement anchors the Friedmann coefficient 1.66 and n/s ≈ 100 (T_c/M_Pl)³ (Gangui, which #11 does not cite). Ruling 13: 'The code checked the arithmetic of a wrong model.'
claims.quote: "An anchor must be independent of the paper. v3's Kibble anchor reproduced v2's own number and so tested nothing.

claims.claim: At minimum production the monopoles close at M* = 2.9–4.4×10¹² GeV, and the 3×10¹³ GeV benchmark is overproduced 2.1×10³–1.2×10⁴ times, scaling as (M/M*)⁴. Computed in v3's own model (f = 1–1.787, hypothesis H, T_c ~ v). Gated; it is a result about a withdrawn model.
claims.quote: At minimum production the abundance closes at M ≈ 2.9–4.4×10¹² GeV [V], and the v3 benchmark of 3×10¹³ GeV is overproduced by 2.1×10³–1.2×10⁴ [V].

claims.claim: Realistic production makes it worse. Starting from the Kibble minimum, annihilation is irrelevant and 4.9×10³–9.8×10⁴ overproduction stands (ξ = 0.76 to 0.5). A colder sector lowers M* to 2.34–3.61×10¹² GeV at ξ = 0.76. The adjudicator accepted these figures without re-running them.
claims.quote: The referee's integration leaves "Omega/Omega_DM = 1.1e12 - 2.2e12" at the benchmark, and LMW's analytic estimate (their eq. 25) gives "1.2e9 - 2.2e11". "Either way the annihilation does not rescue it."

claims.claim: The v3 worklog's F1 found that Kibble with p = 1 fixes a single mass, M* ≈ 3.0×10¹³ GeV, needing dilution 1.3×10¹⁰ at 10¹⁶ GeV. That is superseded: the (M/M*)⁴ conclusion survives, the numbers do not. The referee puts the dilution at 10¹⁶ GeV at 2.6e13 against the corrected M*.
claims.quote: v3 kept the conclusion as "This is a point, not a window."

claims.claim: #11 §12: below about 100 PeV, annihilation in the hidden plasma sets the abundance. That is 'the established topological-dark-matter scenario [28S, 29S], and nothing in it depends on Born reciprocity'. Superheavy masses survive only with a free dilution factor, which removes the mass prediction.
claims.quote: Hidden-sector monopoles avoid overclosing the universe only for symmetry-breaking scales ≲ 100 PeV, or with a period of early matter domination [29S].

claims.claim: Murayama–Shu 2010 [28S]: topological dark matter at 1–10 PeV. Liveoak–Maharana–Wells 2026 [29S]: 'for symmetry-breaking scales >~ 100 PeV, the monopole abundance is unacceptably high'. Both checked at abstract level; no full-text reading is recorded.
claims.quote: "Kibble mechanism drastically underestimates the production of topological defects ... dark matter of mass 1-10 PeV"

claims.claim: The referee listed Baek–Ko–Park (JCAP 2014) and Khoze–Ro (JHEP 2014), 'both: hidden SU(2)->U(1) monopoles + W' + dark photon', as uncited prior art, and the adjudication accepted the list as a to-do.

claims.claim: Round-3 referee: the hidden-sector content, sector separation, ξ and m_ψ are all postulated, and #14 §1 treats the sector as ordinary relativistic QFT. The proposal stands or falls on that literature 'independently of Born reciprocity'. The pre-registration had predicted 'a standard hidden-sector monopole model'.
claims.quote: The DM proposal is the standard hidden 't Hooft-Polyakov-monopole scenario (Baek-Ko-Park 2013; Khoze-Ro 2014; Murayama-Shu 2009; LMW 2026) with one coupling choice (alpha_d = alpha)

claims.claim: Decision 2 (2026-10-19) chose route (c), retirement. Route (b), superheavy plus a named dilution, was rejected: dilution of at least 10³–10⁴. The candidate had earned its place on 'topology makes it stable for free, and the mass came out of the abundance with no free dilution'; round 3 removed the second. Consequence: two program-native candidates plus compatibility with known PeV-scale topological dark matter (candidates/_index.md:31).

claims.claim: #11 §12 verdict: retired as a program-native candidate. The root CLAUDE.md: 'dead as a program-native proposal' and 'merely compatible with known PeV-scale topological dark matter (prior art)'. #11 §13 lists 'superheavy-soliton dark matter (obituary §12)' under 'Withdrawn with cause'.

The wiki's random-walk reading of '√N' is its own, from the name alone (line 57).

claims.claim: Referee: 'Acceptance criterion 3 is not open'; the α_m = 34 regime is exactly Preskill's 1979 Dirac-monopole case (h = 2π/e), and LMW excludes v ≳ 100 PeV. Ruling 10 was upheld at abstract level. Wiki gloss (sqrt-n-floor.md:77): under H the hidden monopoles have the coupling of a Dirac monopole of our own electromagnetism.
claims.quote: Ruling 10, upheld at the level of the abstracts: "Annihilation at α_m ≈ 34 is Preskill's Dirac case, already done for hidden sectors".

claims.claim: The monopole problem: Preskill found annihilation too slow for superheavy monopoles in our plasma. Defects have no n_eq² term, so annihilation only lowers a number set at formation and stops once its rate falls below H (thermal-freeze-out.md:150). A population starting below the annihilation attractor is left as it formed (sqrt-n-floor.md:73; prior-art.md:46).
claims.quote: For superheavy monopoles in our own plasma the classic analysis, Preskill 1979 (#14's [19]), found annihilation too slow to matter, which is why grand-unification monopoles would be overproduced

claims.claim: #14 v3 §3 required inflation to precede the hidden transition, so the monopoles are not inflated away. The referee adds that this needs visible T_RH ≳ v/ξ = 1.06–1.90×10¹² GeV and a two-field or asymmetric reheating (hidden-thermal-history.md:106). After formation, only a later epoch such as early matter domination can dilute superheavy monopoles (#11 §12).
claims.quote: Inflation must precede the hidden transition, and v must lie below the reheating temperature.

claims.claim: #11 §12 'What survives': the minimal adjoint-only sector is excluded on its own terms. With no lighter hidden-charged state, the W′± (thermal, because Kibble production needs a hidden plasma at T ~ v) overclose 10¹⁶–10¹⁷ times at the v3 benchmark. It holds at ξ = 0.76. Gated; benchmark-conditional.
claims.quote: The minimal adjoint-only SU(2) → U(1) hidden sector is excluded on its own terms: its stable W′± overclose the universe by 10¹⁶–10¹⁷ at the v3 benchmark [V].

claims.claim: v3's fix was a light Dirac doublet ψ with U(1)_d charges ±g_d/2. Its charge is the smallest in the sector and sets the monopoles' magnetic charge by Dirac quantization. Hypothesis H matched ψ's charge to the electron's; matching the W′ charge instead gives α_m ~ 137.

history.event: #14 v1 calls the objects 'knots' and fixes their coupling by Dirac quantization against our photon. Round 1 (blind, no code) grades it 'B / medium'. Its valid hits: the coupling argument is self-contradictory; 'knots' becomes 'π₂ monopole-class'; kinetic mixing is unaddressed (v2 adds a postulate and an ε ≲ 10⁻⁵ exclusion). The referee also misread σ_T/M as σ_T, off by about 10⁴³.

#14 v2, 'Dark Matter as Superheavy Magnetic Solitons of a Spontaneously Broken Phase-Space Duality': α_d = 1/(4α) ~ 34 from reciprocity acting as modular S, p = O(1), benchmark 1e16 GeV. Round 2 grades it 'B near B/C / medium', names the α_d derivation the weakest link ('numerology') and leaves seven items pending.
The √N topological-floor argument is made in the chat and never written into any document.
HANDOFF.md still calls superheavy solitons the 'Current best DM candidate', lists the 'trilemma' as open item 8, and queues the √N-floor freeze-out estimate as item 3.

Paul's v3-worklog decisions. F1 moves the benchmark to about 3×10¹³ GeV and keeps 10¹⁶ GeV with ~10¹⁰ dilution as an alternative. F2: 'S-duality is no longer what fixes α_d'; the load-bearing conjecture becomes α_e,d = α, later hypothesis H.

#14 v3 (commit 5dbaa82), 'Dark Matter as Superheavy Monopoles of a Hidden Gauge Sector Selected by a Spontaneously Broken Phase-Space Duality', places the monopole mass 'at about 1e13 to 4e13 GeV with no dilution required'.

Round 3, a blind review with code execution, returns verdict C (16 numerical findings on executed code). The adjudicator rules on 13 findings and upholds the Kibble-normalization finding with an arbitration script.

#14 is withdrawn and moved from papers/ to notes/ with the banner 'Kept as the audit trail; not for circulation'. knot_numbers.py is replaced by verify/soliton_obituary.py, which checks the corrected record.

Round-3 Decisions, delegated by Paul, made by Claude, Paul keeping the veto. Decision 1: strict sector separation. Decision 2: the soliton candidate retired as a program-native proposal (route c). Decision 3: the √N-floor queue item dropped.

#11 v2.1 takes P4 strictly ([27S]), adds the §12 obituary with [V] numbers and lists superheavy-soliton dark matter as 'Withdrawn with cause'. The loophole takes its present wording, 'untested, but has no candidate', replacing the handoff's 'untouched'.

Audit of the wiki-build flags confirms flag 21 (ruling 3's Kibble–Zurek attribution), flag 22 (Planck's N_eff interval), flag 28 (#11 §11.2's formula 4π/e² written beside 34), flag 33 (soliton_obituary.py claims more coverage than it has) and flag 34 (constants typed in without the model-memory caveat).

tensions.description: Loophole open or closed: #11 §12 says the topological clumping loophole 'remains untested, but has no candidate'. #11 §14 item 8 says the 'p-localization items are closed by the §12 obituary'. #11 does not reconcile them. The wiki reads them together (untested, no candidate, no work item), per the conflicts register, and does not decide.

HANDOFF §2 against #11 v2.1. The handoff calls the solitons the 'Current best DM candidate', the loophole 'untouched', and conjugate monopoles 'As ontology ... alive (the soliton candidate)', tying the ontology to the candidate. #11 §11.1 and §12 keep the ontology alive while retiring the candidacy. The wiki follows #11 and marks the handoff's §2 candidate and §8 queue superseded.

Two survivor lists differ. #11 §12 lists the Dirac relation [T], W′ overclosure [V] and the loophole. The adjudication's 'What survives v3' lists the compatibility theorem, the benchmark-conditional arithmetic (flux, densities, σ_T/M, W′), kinetic-mixing points (a) and (c), and the minimal-sector exclusion. #11 does not restate the benchmark arithmetic or point (c).

#11 §11.2 writes 'Dirac's condition e·g ~ 2π pins the magnetic coupling near 4π/e² ≈ 34'. Flag 28 (confirmed by 2 independent checks, 2026-10-22): the number 34 = 1/(4α) is right; 4π/e² = 1/α ≈ 137. #11 line 118 is still uncorrected.

Ceiling or floor: P4 strict writes gravity-induced mixing as ε ≲ 10⁻¹³. The referee notes that Gherghetta et al. present 10⁻¹³ as a minimum ('minimum kinetic mixing in any theory with hidden gauge interactions and charge symmetry breaking'), consistent with '≲' only as 'up to'. Flagged, not resolved.

Gate self-description against coverage (flag 33). The verify/soliton_obituary.py docstring says it recomputes every number the adjudication and §12 quote, and its closing line prints 'every number the round-3 record quotes reproduces'. It does not check the benchmark-conditional arithmetic (flux, densities, σ_T/M), α_m ≈ 34, the referee's Kibble–Zurek and Boltzmann ranges, ruling 6, or ε ~ 1e-7–1e-6. Both claims are still in the script as of this reading.

Ruling 3 attributes '1e9–1e12 overproduction' to the referee's Kibble–Zurek integration. The integration gave 1.1e12–2.2e12; the 1e9 end is the LMW analytic estimate (flag 21). The adjudication still reads that way.

Popular articles against the record. #10 and #12 still present the soliton candidate as live. #12 identifies the momentum-polarized sector as 'the magnetic side of electromagnetism'. The wiki treats both as popsci-only: the identification is dead and contradicts strict sector separation.

readers.summary: Partition F1 treats monopoles almost entirely through the retired soliton candidate (#14): superheavy 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles of a hidden SU(2)_d → U(1)_d sector, magnetically charged under the hidden U(1)_d only, with g_m = 4π/g_d from the hidden sector's own Dirac quantization ("nothing is quantized against our gauge field"). #14 placed that sector in "the momentum-polarized half of a spontaneously broken Born reciprocity", but called the placement "Conjectural", used the charge-lattice/duality-frame correspondence "only as motivation", and said "No numerical result below depends on it". So in these pages the conjugate sector is never the magnetic side of our electromagnetism. It may host its own gauge force and monopoles, kept apart from ours by sector separation, now strict P4 (Decision 1: ε ≲ 10⁻¹³ from gravity, zero if hidden C is gauged). An unbroken U(1)_d gives no visible magnetic flux even with mixing, and strict P4 closes the Witten-effect charge. Round 3 (2026-10-19, verdict C) found p ≈ 104, a floor, so the 3×10¹³ GeV benchmark is overproduced 2.1×10³–1.2×10⁴ [V, gated]. The candidate was retired, "merely compatible" with prior-art PeV-scale topological dark matter. Survivors: the Dirac relation [T], W′ overclosure [V], and a loophole #11 calls both untested and closed. Every attempt to tie the hidden sector's charges or coupling to ours is dead or superseded: Dirac quantization against our photon, v2's "S-dual image of the electric sector", hypothesis H, and popsci #12's "magnetic side of electromagnetism". Alive: "by P4, conjugate-sector solitons gravitate" (#11 §11.1). The χ page never relates χ to monopoles. This partition does not discuss #11 §11.3's [O] enlarged-modular-structure conjecture, Weyl-semimetal Berry monopoles, or App. A items 5 and 11; row 8 appears only by reference. No checked wiki quotation contradicts its document.

tensions.description: The README tagline ('explaining dark matter and missing magnetic monopoles') contradicts #11 §11.1, Appendix A item 5 and HANDOFF §2, which all list the monopole explanation as dead. Flag 37 is confirmed (2026-10-22) and unruled; the README is unchanged since 2026-10-18. The document wins.

HANDOFF keeps the soliton alive. §2 calls it 'Current best DM candidate', ties monopole ontology to 'the soliton candidate', and lists a trilemma and the √N-floor freeze-out; §3 calls #14 v2 'CURRENT'; §8 queues the √N floor. #11 v2.1+ retires the candidate, keeps the ontology without it, and leaves two candidates. Root CLAUDE.md records the candidate dead and §8 item 3 dropped. HANDOFF is a 2026-10-19 record; #11 wins.

Popsci #12 identifies the momentum-polarized sector with 'the magnetic side of electromagnetism', its coupling (~34) fixed by our 1/137, and says the momentum polarization carries the whole magnetic mirror-family. Against it: HANDOFF lists 'α_d ≈ 34 via Dirac quantization against our photon' as dead and calls the candidate 'NOT magnetically charged under our photon'; #11 P4 is strict; §12 retires the solitons; row 7 requires SM decoupling. The 2026-10-26/28 edits left these passages unchanged. Only the wiki notes the conflict; no build flag targets it.

Both popsci articles keep the three-way question with knots or solitons as the third option, and #12 says three requirements 'select the same corner'. #11 §12 and §13 withdraw superheavy-soliton dark matter and keep two candidates.

Acceptance criterion 1 and the electric sublattice. HANDOFF says η must also select the electric sublattice, and #14 v3's criterion (1) asks η to select 'the hidden sector's electric description'. The toy worklog records the referees' wording without that clause, and #11 §14 item 11 and the toy note call the criterion met 'in the referees' wording'. The toy note has no charge-lattice content, and its 'Not shown' list omits the clause. Nothing in the record claims the clause delivered, and nothing lists it as an open end.

Flag 28: #11 §11.2 writes the magnetic coupling as '4π/e² ≈ 34'. The flag, confirmed by two independent checks on 2026-10-22, says the 34 is right and the formula is not: with α = e²/4π, 4π/e² = 1/α ≈ 137, while e·g = 2π gives π/e² = 1/(4α) ≈ 34.26. It is unruled and #11 is unchanged. The check prints only and is not gated. This 34 is our own magnetic coupling, distinct from the dead α_d.

#11 counts 'one structural unification (polarization of phase space and of charge space as one move)' among its products (§15; §1 says it 'turns out to be the same mathematical move'). §11.3 tags only the shared-matrix identification [D — structural; math T] and the joint modular structure 'Conjecture [O]', and §14 item 8 lists formalizing 'the unification' as open. §15's wording does not separate the two.

Clumping-loophole wording. §12 says the topological loophole 'remains untested, but has no candidate', and Appendix A item 3 calls it untested. §14 item 8 says the 'p-localization items are closed by the §12 obituary'. 'Closed' there refers to the open-problems list; the loophole itself stays untested.

Row 8 lists a 'Permanent null' for our magnetic monopoles as a program requirement, killed by direct detection. §11.1 attributes the null result to inflationary dilution [T] and declares the program's explanation dead, and the row gives no program-internal derivation. This is not necessarily a contradiction, but the basis of the requirement is unstated.

Terminology: round 1 renamed 'knots' to 'π₂ monopole-class' in #14 v2. #11's §12 plain passage, §15 and Appendix A item 5, and both popsci articles, still call the 't Hooft–Polyakov monopole candidate 'knots'.

readers.summary:
Partition A covers #11 v2.2, HANDOFF, README, root CLAUDE.md, both popsci articles and three papers. The toy note, #13 and the diameter note have no monopole content.

#11 treats monopoles in three layers.

1. The founding idea that conjugate-space monopoles explain our null result is dead: 'the relevant duality is electric–magnetic … not x↔p, and inflationary dilution already accounts for absence' (§11.1). As ontology they stay 'alive and consequence-bearing', because by P4 conjugate-sector solitons gravitate. Row 8 requires a permanent null for our monopoles, with Berry-curvature monopoles in Weyl semimetals as the only shadow.
2. The dark-matter candidate, superheavy 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles of a hidden, p-local SU(2) → U(1) sector (#14), was retired on 2026-10-19. One defect per Hubble volume gives p ≈ 104, so the 3×10¹³ GeV benchmark is overproduced 2.1×10³–1.2×10⁴ times [V, gated], and the viable sub-100-PeV version is prior art. What survives: a weakly coupled hidden sector always has strongly coupled monopoles (Dirac quantization [T]); W′ overclosure excludes the adjoint-only sector [V]; the topological clumping loophole is untested and has no candidate.
3. The DSZ pairing makes the charge lattice symplectic, a duality frame is a Lagrangian polarization, and S-duality uses ρ's matrix [D — structural; math T]. Joining P5's polarization and the charge-lattice polarization in 'one enlarged modular structure' is a conjecture [O], and it is not queued.

On comatter, the current record keeps the sectors apart. P4 is strict (gauge forces do not cross polarizations), HANDOFF's candidate was 'dark by sector separation, NOT magnetically charged under our photon', and 'α_d ≈ 34 via Dirac quantization against our photon' is dead. Only the unrevised popsci #12 still calls the momentum-polarized sector 'the magnetic side of electromagnetism'; #10 and the README tagline also predate the obituary. The toy note never addresses HANDOFF's 'selecting the electric sublattice' clause.

The hidden sector was the momentum-polarized half of broken Born reciprocity and was conjectured to be the S-dual image of the electric sector. One vacuum event would then fix both the x/p asymmetry and the electric/magnetic asymmetry of the observed spectrum. In this wording the conjugate sector is itself the magnetic (S-dual) image of ours.

claims.quote: the hidden sector is the momentum-polarized half of a spontaneously broken Born reciprocity and is conjectured to be the S-dual image of the electric sector
"Magnetic" refers throughout to the sector's duality-frame character - solitonic, strongly coupled - not to a charge visible to our electromagnetism.

history.event: #1 v0.1 contains row 8: monopoles a permanent null '(p-polarized solitons)', with Berry-curvature monopoles in solids as the only shadow. Addenda v0.2-v0.6 add no monopole content beyond v0.2's 'rows 7-9 (permanent nulls)'.

#9 v1.0 keeps row 8 without '(p-polarized solitons)'. #11 v2.0 then adds §11 (monopole audit, full dual spectrum, symplectic charge lattice, [O] conjecture), the §12 knot trilemma, Appendix A items 3, 5 and 11, and '(ours)' in row 8.

#14 review rounds 1-2:
- Round 1 (verdict B) found the α_d-from-our-DSZ contradiction; v2 restated it as the reciprocity-as-S conjecture.
- Round 1 also renamed 'knots' to π₂ monopole-class and added a kinetic-mixing postulate with an ε ≲ 10⁻⁵ exclusion.
- Round 2 (verdict B near B/C) named the α_d derivation the weakest link ('matrix coincidence ≠ physical identity' / 'numerology').
Initial commit: the README describes the repo as a 'Physics hypothesis explaining dark matter and missing magnetic monopoles'. The line has never been edited.
Import from claude.ai of #1, #9, #11 v2.0, HANDOFF, and #14 v2 ('Dark Matter as Superheavy Magnetic Solitons of a Spontaneously Broken Phase-Space Duality').

Restructure: #14 placed in papers/ as a current reference; #1, #9 and the calc notes moved to notes/. Since then the monopole text in notes/ has not changed except by #14's later move (git log -S monopol -- notes/ shows only 008c3ee and 5b6efaa), and HANDOFF's monopole text not at all (only 8d588f6).

verify/knot_numbers.py recomputes every #14 v2 number, and all reproduce. Its NOTE lines record that running α moves 34 to about 29, that the extended Parker excess is about 7 orders, that the mass window is not Kibble-only, and that the mass formula's coupling contradicts §2.
Literature check: with a massless dark photon, kinetic mixing gives the dark monopole no visible magnetic flux (Hiramatsu et al. 2021), so v2's ε·g exclusion premise is wrong in four places.
Paul accepts F1/F2: the benchmark moves to 3×10¹³ GeV, and the sector is read as weakly coupled with strongly coupled solitons. O3 is logged: #14 and #13 differ on the dark sector's kinematics.
verify/dark_sector.py: the adjoint-only SU(2)_d → U(1)_d sector leaves stable W′± at 10¹⁶-10¹⁷ times the observed density, so a light doublet is needed; ξ < 0.77.
Round 3 pre-registered: expected verdict B, weakest link 'framework does no work'.

Round 3 adjudicated, verdict C on the Kibble normalization (p ≈ 104, not 0.023). #14 gets a 'failed review' banner, and scripts/check.sh fails on v3's affected claims by design. The pre-registration missed.

tensions.description: README.md:2 still calls the program an explanation of 'missing magnetic monopoles'. #11 §11.1 ('As an explanation of the null result: dead'), Appendix A item 5 and HANDOFF §2 all record that explanation as dead. Flag 37 was confirmed on 2026-10-22, but its ruling checkboxes are blank. The documents win.

#1's row 8 grounds the monopole null in '(p-polarized solitons)', the conjugate-space explanation #11 rules dead. #9 and #11 dropped the gloss without putting another reason in the row. #11 row 8 still lists 'Permanent null' under 'Program requirement', with kill condition 'Direct detection'. Yet §11.1 credits the absence to inflationary dilution [T] rather than to the program, and the wiki summary glosses the row 'The absence is already explained by inflation'.

How far the magnetic sector is identified with the conjugate sector differs across versions:
- #14 v2 (git only): the p-polarized hidden sector is 'conjectured to be the S-dual image of the electric sector', with reciprocity acting as S on the coupling.
- #11 v2.0 §12 (git only): knots are 'the conjugate sector's monopoles'.
- #14 v3: the hidden sector is only 'identified with the momentum-polarized half', the charge lattice used 'only as motivation', and no exact electric-magnetic duality assumed.
- HANDOFF.md:26: 'dark by sector separation,' NOT magnetically charged under our photon.
- #11 now: conjugate-sector solitons alive as ontology (§11.1), and one modular structure for both polarizations only an [O] conjecture (§11.3).
The current documents win.

Two different '≈ 34's:
- #11 §11.2's coupling of our own magnetic world, '4π/e² ≈ 34' [T]. Flag 28 says the number is right but the formula is the 137 one.
- #14's α_d / α_m = 1/(4α) ≈ 34 for hidden monopoles, which HANDOFF §2 and the wiki (e21f607) call dead.
Flag 28 itself notes that the two are distinct.

HANDOFF §6 records the round-2 referee's claim that running α drags 34 'toward ~6–8'. The repo's recomputation and #14 v3 give about 29 at 10¹² GeV, 'not to the referee's 6-8'. The later recomputation supersedes HANDOFF's record.
#14 v3 and commits d15cd4a/5dbaa82 state ξ < 0.77. Round-3 ruling 5 and the gated verify/soliton_obituary.py give ξ < 0.760. #14 is withdrawn, so the gated value stands.

It still names superheavy π₂ monopole-class solitons the 'Current best DM candidate' and conjugate monopoles 'alive (the soliton candidate)'. #11 v2.1 §12 and the root CLAUDE.md record that candidate as retired on 2026-10-19. The document (#11) wins.

claims.claim: Inflation after a GUT symmetry-breaking transition removes the superheavy monopoles that transition would overproduce (Preskill 1979); this is the standard resolution of the monopole problem and one of inflation's motivations (Guth 1981 †). tensions.description: Inside #11: §12 says the topological clumping loophole 'remains untested, but has no candidate', while §14 item 8 says the p-localization items are 'closed by the §12 obituary'. Not reconciled; the wiki treats it as open with no work item.
Inside #11: §11.1 calls 'true but irrelevant' 'the empty set (a correction supplied by P.R.)'; Appendix A item 5 quotes P.R. as 'measure zero'. Same verdict either way.
Flag 28 (confirmed, awaiting ruling): #11 §11.2 says Dirac's condition 'pins the magnetic coupling near 4π/e² ≈ 34', but 4π/e² = 1/α ≈ 137; 34 is π/e² = 1/(4α). The wiki quotes #11 as written.
DSZ normalization: #11 and #14 write the pairing in 2πℤ, while Zwanziger's abstract states 4πℤ (ruling 12, minor). The choice moves the magnetic coupling between 34.26 and 137.04.
HANDOFF §2 ties the surviving monopole ontology to the soliton candidate; #11 v2.1 keeps the ontology and retires the candidacy. Settled by precedence for #11.
README.md still says the program explains 'missing magnetic monopoles'; HANDOFF §2 and #11 §11.1 list that explanation as dead (flag 37, awaiting ruling).

Popsci #12 identifies the momentum-polarized sector with 'the magnetic side of electromagnetism'. This conflicts with strict P4, row 7, the dead α_d ≈ 34 via our photon, and #14's 'dark by sector separation'. Popsci never decides status, and the wiki records the claim as dead.

The summary (wiki) and #11 frame row 8 differently. The summary says row 8's null 'already has the standard explanation' and 'is already explained by inflation'. #11 §13 gives the row's standard expectation as 'Model-dependent' and does not call the row non-discriminating; the summary's reading draws on §11.1. Separately, #11 §11.2 says the magnetic mirror family's non-observation is 'structural' (strong coupling, 'heavy and bound'). Neither the summary nor the status pages carry that clause. The document wins.

Textual point: #11 §11.1 attaches the Weyl-semimetal Berry-curvature monopoles, as 'laboratory shadow', to conjugate-sector solitons, while §13 row 8 calls them 'the only shadow' of 'Magnetic monopoles (ours)'. The alive register follows the row, and the glossary calls them 'the one laboratory analog of momentum-space monopoles that row 8 names'.

Ruling 3 credits '1e9–1e12 overproduction' to the referee's Kibble–Zurek integration. That integration gave 1.1e12–2.2e12; the 1e9 lower end is LMW's analytic estimate (flag 21). The verdict is unaffected.

verify/soliton_obituary.py says every number of the round-3 record reproduces, but it does not check the referee's figures (rulings 3, 4, 6) or the surviving flux and density arithmetic (flag 33). Its constants are typed in, not retrieved (flag 34).

Inside #14: the first-order gravitational-wave paragraph (bubble counting p ~ 104(β/H)³ = 1e2–1e8) is 'flatly inconsistent' with §3's p = 1 taken as the upper end of the Kibble yield. It died with the manuscript.

#14 describes the dark sector entirely in ordinary kinematics, while #13 labels conjugate quanta by an invariant length. The two were never reconciled; #11 governs for χ.
HANDOFF §1 says three blind reviews returned verdict B. Its §6 records two completed rounds on the monopole manuscript #14 (B; B near B/C) and a third that was incomplete.

readers.summary:
Partition F2 records monopoles in three places.

1. **Our own sector.** Founding supposition 5 held that monopoles live in conjugate space, which would explain why none is seen. As an explanation it is dead. #11 §11.1 [D]: "the relevant duality is electric–magnetic (E↔B, g → 1/g), not x↔p", and inflationary dilution [T] already accounts for the absence. Row 8 keeps a permanent null, with Berry-curvature monopoles in Weyl semimetals [16†] as "the only shadow". The README still says the program explains "missing magnetic monopoles" (flag 37).

2. **Comatter.** The record keeps the magnetic side of our electromagnetism separate from the p-polarized sector.
   - As ontology, conjugate-sector solitons are alive [D], because "by P4, conjugate-sector solitons gravitate".
   - Strict P4 ("gauge forces do not cross polarizations"; ε ≲ 10⁻¹³ [27S]) closed the Witten-effect channel.
   - The hidden sector was "dark by sector separation", not magnetically charged under our photon.
   - α_d ≈ 34 via Dirac quantization against our photon is dead.
   - #12's "momentum-polarized sector is the magnetic side of electromagnetism" is popsci-only, and the wiki records it as dead.

   #14 and #11 v2.0 did identify a hidden SU(2)→U(1) monopole sector with the momentum-polarized half. Round 3 killed that candidate: one defect per Hubble volume gives p ≈ 104 [V], not 0.023, and the benchmark is overproduced 2.1×10³–1.2×10⁴ times [V]. Its version with v ≲ 100 PeV is prior art, to which the framework "adds nothing testable". W′ overclosure survives [V]. The √N floor is dead. The topological loophole is untested and has no candidate.

3. **The formal link.** The DSZ charge lattice is symplectic, and choosing a duality frame is choosing a Lagrangian polarization [D — structural; math T]; S-duality and ρ share one matrix. One enlarged modular structure is a conjecture [O] (OP8, not queued), and the electric-sublattice clause is unaddressed. Flag 28: #11 §11.2's 34 is the right number beside the wrong formula (4π/e² = 1/α ≈ 137; 34 = 1/(4α)).

The summary and status pages match #11 §§11–12, with two exceptions. They frame row 8 as already explained by inflation, where #11 §13 says "Model-dependent". And they omit §11.2's "structural" account of why the magnetic mirror family is not observed.

Above it the abundance scales as (M/M*)⁴, so dilution of 1.3e6 is needed at 1e15, 1.3e10 at 1e16 and 1.3e14 at 1e17 GeV. The worklog took horizon counting to give p ≈ 0.023, moving M* to 7.7e13. claims.claim: Worklog F2: v2 used e_d²/4π ≈ 1/137 for the mass in §3 but alpha_d = 34 in §2 and §4; with 34, the solitons would not be heavy. The self-consistent reading: the dual elementary coupling α_e,d is weak, the solitons are heavy, and the solitons are strongly coupled (α_m ≈ 1/(4α_e,d)). alpha_d ≈ 34 then follows from the mirror-coupling equality α_e,d ≈ α. Minicharged, confined monopoles need a massive dark photon. So v2's premise that mixing gives the solitons magnetic charge εg under our photon is wrong, in four places. The real leakage: dark electric states acquire a millicharge εe, and CP violation gives the monopoles a small visible electric charge. Parker and MACRO stay only to show what monopoles of our U(1) would do.

claims.claim: Worklog O1: in the minimal SU(2)_d → U(1)_d model with only the adjoint Higgs, W′± is the lightest dark-charged state and is stable. Kibble production needs a hot dark plasma, so W′± are thermal, and their relic is 0.8–15e16 times the observed density: the model is excluded. The fix is at least one light dark doublet. That fermion is itself a relic (worklog: all of DM at 0.3–1.0 TeV, 10% at 0.1–0.3 TeV, later corrected), and its plasma runs Preskill-type monopole annihilation. Computed at ξ = 1 only. The W′ exclusion survives.
claims.quote: **O1 — dark W′± fate: fatal to the minimal model, not to the candidate**

claims.quote: An exact mirror copy of the SM has no stable monopoles (π₂(S³) = 0), so H relates couplings only, not gauge groups.

claims.claim: v3 abstract: dark matter is superheavy 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles of a hidden SU(2) broken to U(1), and the hidden sector is identified with the momentum-polarized half of broken Born reciprocity. One coupling hypothesis plus the hidden sector's own Dirac quantization gives α_m = 1/(4α) ≈ 34, and Kibble production puts the mass at 1e13–4e13 GeV 'with no dilution required'. The candidate is stable by topology, dark by sector separation, collisionless and beyond direct detection. It requires a light hidden fermion (without it the W′ overclose by 1e16–1e17) and a hidden temperature ratio ξ ≤ 0.77.
claims.quote: The hidden sector is identified with the momentum-polarized half of a spontaneously broken Born reciprocity.

claims.claim: v3's hidden sector, postulated: the momentum-polarized matter sector contains SU(2)_d with a real adjoint Φ whose vev v breaks it to U(1)_d. U(1)_d stays unbroken, so the hidden photon is massless; the W′± have mass g_d v. At least one Dirac doublet ψ carries U(1)_d charges ±g_d/2.

claims.quote: The momentum-polarized matter sector contains a gauge group SU(2)_d with a real adjoint scalar Phi whose expectation value v breaks it to U(1)_d.

Any weakly coupled hidden sector therefore has strongly coupled monopoles: this is generic, not a hypothesis. #11 §12 keeps it as a survivor [T].
claims.quote: Any weakly coupled hidden sector therefore has strongly coupled monopoles: the strong magnetic coupling is generic, not a hypothesis.
claims.topic: Dirac quantization in the hidden sector

claims.claim: Hypothesis H, v3's single coupling hypothesis: the smallest hidden charge equals ours, (g_d/2)²/4π = α. Its motivation: reciprocity exchanges the two polarizations, and if it acts on gauge couplings at all, the minimal action equates the elementary charges. Then α_W′ = 4α ≈ 1/34 and α_m = 1/(4α) ≈ 34. Matching the W′ charge instead gives ≈137, and matching at 1e12 GeV ≈29. Without H, α_m is free but necessarily strong; 'H only selects a point'.
claims.quote: The motivation is that reciprocity exchanges the two polarizations; if it acts on gauge couplings at all, the minimal action is to equate the elementary charges of the two sectors.

claims.claim: v3, 'What is not asserted': the monopoles carry no charge under our photon. The Dirac quantization used is the hidden sector's own, and nothing is quantized against our gauge field. Exact electric-magnetic duality is not assumed (it is tested only in N=4 SYM and certain finite N=2 theories); the monopole physics used is semiclassical, at α_W′ ~ 1/34.
claims.quote: These objects carry no charge under our photon. The Dirac quantization used above is the hidden sector's own, applied to its own charges; nothing is quantized against our gauge field.

claims.claim: v3 sector separation, postulated: no field is charged under both U(1)_d and our hypercharge. (a) Pure gravity: kinetic mixing vanishes to all perturbative orders if hidden C is exact; if C is broken, gravity induces it only at six loops or more, giving ε ≲ 1e-13. This is the literature point (a) that survives round 3, and the basis of strict P4.

A gauged discrete symmetry acting as hidden C would forbid it. Round 3 ruled the O(1) coefficient unsupported (ruling 7).
claims.quote: For an O(1) coefficient at the Planck or reduced Planck scale, epsilon ~ 1e-7 to 1e-6.

claims.claim: v3 point (c): with U(1)_d unbroken, kinetic mixing gives the monopoles no magnetic charge under our photon and no visible magnetic flux. Minicharged monopoles would need a massive hidden photon, which v3 excludes. The visible leakage is instead ψ's electric charge ~εe and, with CP violation, a small visible electric charge on the monopoles. The no-flux point survives (literature point (c)). v3's further conclusion that the decisive constraints act on ψ and not on the dark matter was killed by ruling 9.

claims.claim: SU(2)_d → U(1)_d has π₂(SU(2)/U(1)) = π₂(S²) = Z and supports 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles, stable by topological charge. Their mass is M = 4πf v/g_d, with f = 1 in the BPS limit rising to about 1.79 at large scalar self-coupling; under H, M ≈ (21–37) v. The referee's own boundary-value solution gives f = 1.7867; v3 leaves the 1.79 uncited.

claims.claim: Negative result: the minimal adjoint-only hidden sector fails. Its W′± are the lightest hidden-charged states, stable by U(1)_d charge, and thermally populated by the plasma that Kibble production needs. They freeze out at 1e16–1e17 times the DM density. This survives round 3 and is gated.
claims.quote: Standard freeze-out [17] then leaves them at 1e16 to 1e17 times the observed dark-matter density, bracketing the annihilation coefficient over a factor of ten. The adjoint-only sector is excluded.

claims.claim: v3's fix is the Dirac doublet ψ: W′+ decays to a ψ pair, and ψ, stable by U(1)_d charge, annihilates to hidden photons. Under H, v3 says ψ is under 10% of DM for m_ψ below 0.1–0.3 TeV and all of it at 0.3–1 TeV, and adopts MeV < m_ψ < 0.1 TeV. The ψ plasma is the medium for monopole–antimonopole annihilation. Ruling 4 corrected the window; ruling 6 raised the lower mass to ≳ 20–30 MeV.

claims.quote: Under H, psi makes up less than 10% of the dark matter for m_psi below 0.1-0.3 TeV, and all of it at 0.3-1 TeV.

That gives M* ~ (0.9–3.7)e13 GeV, which the reduced-Planck convention would lower by ~3. Benchmark: M = 3e13 GeV, v ~ (0.8–1.4)e12 GeV.
claims.quote: One monopole per horizon volume with g* = 100 gives p ~ 0.023; we take p = 1 as the upper end.

Annihilation runs through the hidden plasma (ψ and hidden photons) at α_m ~ 34, where Sommerfeld enhancement and bound states may matter, and needs a dedicated strong-coupling freeze-out (acceptance criterion 3). Inflation must precede the hidden transition, and v must lie below the reheating temperature. Ruling 10 says criterion 3 is not open: it is Preskill's Dirac case, already done for hidden sectors.
claims.quote: Here annihilation runs through the hidden plasma (psi and hidden photons) at alpha_m ~ 34, where Sommerfeld enhancement and rapid bound-state formation may matter.

claims.claim: v3 benchmark arithmetic at M = 3e13 GeV: mean n ~ 4.2e-20 /cm³; at the local density (0.4 GeV/cm³) one monopole per ~0.075 km³, spacing ~420 m, drifting at ~1e-3 c. The referee confirms it, and it survives as benchmark-conditional arithmetic.
claims.quote: At the local halo density (0.4 GeV/cm^3) there is one monopole per ~0.075 km^3, a mean spacing of about 420 m, drifting at ~1e-3 c.

claims.claim: 'Not monopoles of our U(1)': with magnetic charge under our electromagnetism they would be classic monopoles, and excluded. Their flux, F = nv/4π ~ 3e-8 /cm²/s/sr, would exceed the Parker bound (~1e-15 for M ≲ 1e17 GeV) by 7.5 orders, MACRO (2.8e-16 for m ≳ 1e10 GeV) by eight and extended Parker by twelve. Sector separation is therefore mandatory, and §2(c) shows kinetic mixing does not undo it while U(1)_d is unbroken. The referee confirms the numbers; they survive as benchmark-conditional arithmetic.

claims.quote: If these objects carried magnetic charge under our electromagnetism, they would be classic monopoles and excluded.

claims.claim: v3 dark radiation: the hidden photon is radiation. If the hidden sector (SU(2)_d gauge fields, adjoint, one ψ doublet) shared our temperature above v, it would add ΔN_eff ~ 0.86, which is excluded. It must therefore be reheated to ξ < 0.77, an assumption the framework does not fix. A colder sector lowers M* by ξ^(3/4) (~0.8). Ruling 5 corrected the bound to ξ < 0.760.
claims.quote: The proposal therefore requires the hidden sector to have been reheated to xi < 0.77 of our temperature, an assumption about reheating that the framework does not fix.

claims.claim: Monopole–monopole scattering through the hidden photon is Rutherford-like at α_m ~ 34 but suppressed by the mass: σ_T/M ~ 1e-26 cm²/g. The candidate is effectively collisionless CDM, so dwarf-galaxy cores must be baryonic. The referee confirms this up to a factor-2 convention, but notes that 'effectively collisionless' rests on two-body σ_T only; collective magnetic-plasma effects are unevaluated.
claims.quote: The candidate is effectively collisionless cold dark matter, so observed dwarf-galaxy cores must be attributed to baryonic feedback.

claims.claim: v3's exclusion conditions that bear on monopoles: (1) any confirmed non-gravitational coupling of the dominant DM component to the SM; (2) any confirmed monopole flux of our U(1) at DM abundance; (3) exclusion of the millicharged ψ window, which lapses if hidden C is gauged; (4) a strong-coupling relic calculation showing annihilation at α_m ~ 34 cannot leave the observed abundance.
claims.quote: 2. Any confirmed magnetic-monopole flux of our U(1) at dark-matter abundance.

Requirements forced by consistency: (i) a hidden doublet fermion between the MeV scale and ~0.1 TeV; (ii) ξ < 0.77; (iii) an unbroken U(1)_d.
claims.quote: the identification of the SU(2)_d sector as the momentum-polarized matter sector;

claims.claim: Referee: one monopole per H⁻³ is p = 104.3 at g* = 100 (24.9 per (4π/3)H⁻³). v3's 0.0228 = 45/(2π²·100) is the H³ abundance with the factor (1.66√g*)³ = 4576 dropped. One per horizon is a causal lower bound (Gangui; LMW; Kibble–Zurek adds more), so p should be ≥ ~25–100, not ≤ 1.

claims.claim: Referee: the corrected Kibble-minimum M* is 2.87–4.44e12 GeV at ξ = 1 and 2.34–3.61e12 GeV at ξ = 0.76. The 3e13 benchmark is overproduced 2.1e3–2.7e4 times, so 'no dilution required' fails. v3's own first-order GW scenario (f*/H* = 1–100) implies bubble counting p ~ 104(β/H)³ = 1e2–1e8, inconsistent with 'p = 1 as the upper end'.

claims.claim: Referee: Kibble–Zurek production (n ~ λHT_c²) followed by diffusive and radiative capture (LMW's equations) at v3's own parameters gives Ω/Ω_DM ≈ 1.1e12–2.2e12; LMW's analytic eq. 25 gives 1.2e9–2.2e11. The Kibble-minimum yield lies far below the annihilation attractor, so annihilation is irrelevant there. Acceptance criterion 3 is not open: α_m = 34 is exactly Preskill's Dirac-monopole case, and LMW 2026 excludes hidden monopoles for v ≳ 100 PeV.
claims.quote: the "strong-coupling" regime alpha_m = 34 is exactly the Dirac-monopole case of Preskill 1979 (h = 2 pi/e); its modern hidden-sector version (LMW 2026) excludes v >~ 100 PeV for hidden monopoles.

Such fields are exactly what sector separation excludes, so v3's ε ~ 1e-7–1e-6 contradicts its own postulate (ruling 7, upheld). The referee also said Baumgart et al. lack the operator; ruling 8 overturned that from their footnote 5.

claims.claim: Referee: a hidden θ is physical (ψ is massive) and generically O(1). With mixing, the DM monopoles acquire a visible electric charge q_vis ~ χθ_d/(2π)·e (BJK eq. 3.19): 1.6e-8 e at χ = 1e-7 to 1.6e-7 e at χ = 1e-6, for θ = 1. The monopoles are hidden dyons, so exclusion condition 1 triggers itself whenever ε ≠ 0. Ruling 9 accepted this without a re-check; decision 1's strict P4 closes the channel.

claims.quote: 8. Hidden theta / Witten effect (4a.7): monopoles are hidden dyons; visible charge ~1e-8-1e-7 e for eps~1e-7-1e-6.

claims.claim: Referee's literature check: an unbroken U(1)_d gives no visible magnetic flux (Brümmer–Jaeckel p.5, 'hidden monopoles are invisible to ordinary electrically charged matter'; Hiramatsu et al.). With a massive dark photon, dark magnetic charges acquire an εe/4π coupling to the massless photon and are confined by flux tubes (Terning–Verhaaren p.11).

claims.claim: Decision 1, strict sector separation: ε ≲ 1e-13 from gravity alone, and zero if hidden charge conjugation is gauged. This is P4 at face value. P4 (#11 §4) says matter comes in x-polarized (SM) and p-polarized (χ) representations, both coupling universally to H, and gauge forces do not cross polarizations; strict since v2.1. The alternative rested on an unsourced coefficient. Strict P4 closes three failure channels: the ψ millicharge, the monopoles' Witten-effect charge and re-thermalization of the hidden sector. Claude decided under Paul's delegation; Paul keeps the veto.

claims.claim: Decision 2: the soliton candidate is retired as a program-native proposal (route c). Route (a), v ≲ 100 PeV, works, but it is Murayama–Shu's and LMW's model and nothing in it depends on Born reciprocity. Route (b), superheavy plus a named dilution, is rejected: it needs a free dilution factor of at least 1e3–1e4, the mass stops being a prediction, and 'the program does not trade falsifiability for survival'. The trilemma becomes two candidates (gated χ particles; the X-condensate), plus compatibility with known PeV-scale topological DM.
