tensions.description: Baumgart et al. 0901.0283: the referee says the paper does not support the adjoint dimension-5 operator. The adjudication overturns this (ruling 8), quoting their footnote 5 verbatim. The adjudication governs.

ψ window: the referee's Boltzmann integration gives 10% of DM at 28–46 GeV and 100% at 96–153 GeV; the adjudicator's gated recount gives 45–49 and 146–158 GeV. The adjudication calls this agreement within ×1.6, and both reject v3's 0.1–0.3 TeV.

Kibble–Zurek overproduction: the referee's own integration gives Ω/Ω_DM ≈ 1.1–2.2e12, and LMW's analytic formula 1.2e9–2.2e11. Ruling 3 summarizes this as '1e9–1e12' and says the integration was not re-run. No gated number covers realistic production; #11 §12 says only that it 'lowers the viable mass much further'.

HANDOFF §6 records round 2's 'α at transition scale drags 34 toward ~6–8' as a valid hit. The v3 worklog finds it not reproduced for the EM coupling (6–8 appears only for 1/(4α₃)); the valid core is a factor-4 convention dependence.
v2 internal: the mass relation M ~ (4π/e_d²)Λ_c ~ 100 Λ_c uses a weak coupling (~1/137), while §2 and §4 use alpha_d ≈ 34, which would make the factor 0.029 (worklog F2).

v2 says irreducible mixing gives the solitons an effective magnetic charge εg under our photon (§2, §4, exclusion 3, criterion 2). The literature report (L1: Hiramatsu et al.; Brümmer–Jaeckel) says an unbroken dark U(1), which is v2's own setup, gives no QED magnetic flux.

v3 §2(a) has gravity-only mixing at ≲ 1e-13, with mixing otherwise requiring bi-charged matter; §2(b) has an O(1) Planck-suppressed dimension-5 coefficient, ε ~ 1e-7–1e-6. The cited sources generate (b) only from bi-charged states, which sector separation forbids. Ruling 7: 'Sec. 2(a) and 2(b) of v3 are in tension'.

v3 §2(c) concludes that the decisive constraints act on ψ, not on the dark matter, and exclusion condition 1 treats any DM–SM coupling as fatal. Yet §2(c)(ii) and BJK give the monopoles a visible electric charge whenever ε ≠ 0 (the Witten effect, ruling 9). Strict P4 (decision 1) removes that branch.

v3 takes p = 1 as the upper end of Kibble production, but one defect per Hubble volume is the causal minimum (ruling 3). v3's own first-order GW paragraph (f*/H* = 1–100) implies bubble counting with p ~ 1e2–1e8.

v3 treats the reduced-Planck convention as lowering M* 'by a factor of about 3', a spread in the band. Ruling 2 says it is not a convention spread: consistently normalized, the two conventions agree (gated). The referee notes that v3's reduced-Planck variant (2.74e12) is in fact the correct Kibble minimum (2.87e12).

v3 §6 says all numerical statements in Secs. 2–4 were computed by executed code. Ruling 13 upholds the objection that this overstates: the code checked the arithmetic of a wrong model. The wrong p first appears as a [V] item in worklog F1 ('horizon-counting p is ≈ 0.023') and passed a circular anchor.
HANDOFF §2 and §8 frame Kibble as a 'ceiling', with the √N floor below it. Ruling 3 inverts this (Kibble is a floor), and decision 3 drops the √N item.

HANDOFF, a snapshot from the handoff, still calls the soliton candidate the 'Current best DM candidate' and #14 v2 the 'CURRENT blind-review manuscript'. The later record withdraws #14 and retires the candidate, and the later documents govern.

#11 §12's plain-language passage calls the objects 'topological knots' and 'heavy knots'. Round 1 renamed 'knots' to π₂ monopole-class, and v2 calls them 'not knot solitons in the pi_3/Hopfion sense'. The file names still say 'knot'.

Mild, cross-reference: #11 §12 says the clumping loophole 'remains untested, but has no candidate', while #11 §14 item 8 says the soliton-spectrum and p-localization items 'are closed by the §12 obituary'. Possibly reconcilable: an open problem closed for want of a candidate, while the loophole itself stays untested.
The round-3 pre-registration cites HANDOFF §6 for rounds 1–2 having been pre-registered and scoring 2 for 2; that statement is in HANDOFF §5.

The adjudication says each of the referee's 16 numerical findings rests on executed code. But step4c.out (T_RH ≳ 1.06–1.90e12 GeV) and step4d.out (reduced-Planck p = 0.828) have no script in review/round3/referee/ or anywhere in git history. 0.828 is independently reproduced (round3_arb.py; gated); the T_RH values are not.

readers.summary: Partition B is the story of #14, the program's monopole dark-matter proposal. v1 (claude.ai) took α_d ≈ 34 from Dirac quantization against our photon. Round 1 (B/medium) killed that ('can't use our DSZ lattice and then deny coupling to our photon') and renamed the 'knots' π₂ monopole-class solitons. v2 conjectured that 'the momentum-polarized matter sector is the S-dual image of the electric sector', with reciprocity acting as modular S on the coupling to give α_d = 1/(4α) ≈ 34; 'magnetic' meant duality-frame character, 'not a charge visible to our electromagnetism'. Round 2 (B near B/C) called that the weakest link ('numerology'). v3 dropped S.
